title: Third pillar of Iman – belief in the books
intro: “Wa kutubihi” – and I believe in Allah’s Books.

learn.html: Allah’s Books are the revelations that Allah, the Most High, sent to His prophets through the angel Jibril. They contain guidance, advice and rules for how people should live. Every Muslim must believe in Allah’s Books. They are divided into the big books (kutub) and the small scrolls (suhuf).

The Qur’an mentions the scrolls (suhuf) of Ibrahim (AS) and Musa (AS). Ibn Hibban reports that 50 scrolls were revealed to Shith (AS), 30 to Idris (AS), 10 to Ibrahim (AS) and 10 to Musa (AS) before the Tawrat.

learn.alt: An open, decorated copy of the Qur’an on a stand

learn.html: The Qur’an is Allah’s last revelation, revealed to Allah’s last Prophet, Muhammad (SAW). Its revelation began on Laylat al-Qadr, in the month of Ramadan, in the year 610, in the cave of Hira on the mountain of Nur. It was revealed over 23 years – 13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah. The Qur’an has 114 surahs and 6,236 ayat, and it is divided into 30 juz’.

questions.q: What is the third pillar of Iman?
options: Wa kutubihi – belief in Allah’s Books
Wa malaa’ikatihi – belief in the angels
Wal-yawmil-aakhiri – belief in the Last Day
Wa rusulihi – belief in the messengers
